question: persister
prompt:
Research question: "What measurements or analyses would best reveal why a small fraction of genetically identical cancer cells survive targeted drug treatment?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

Work in two steps. First, in the candidates field, brainstorm 20 candidate ideas, one line each, covering as wide a range as you can. Then select the 5 candidates that best combine being non-obvious with being feasible and informative, and develop those as your ideas.

ideas.title: Lineage barcoding with drug challenge and transcriptomic readout
ideas.description: Label each founder cell with a unique heritable barcode, expose the population to the drug, and sequence barcodes plus transcriptomes of survivors. This tests whether survivors arise from a few pre-existing clones or from stochastic, independent cell-level switches, and whether survivor states are inherited.

ideas.title: Pre-treatment apoptotic priming by BH3 profiling
ideas.description: Measure each subpopulation's mitochondrial apoptotic priming with BH3 profiling before drug exposure, then sort high- and low-priming cells and challenge each with the drug. If survival tracks priming, tolerance is set by a pre-existing mitochondrial threshold, not by drug-specific pathways.

ideas.title: Per-cell drug accumulation and efflux measurement
ideas.description: Quantify intracellular drug concentration in single cells using a fluorescent analog or mass-spec imaging, paired with efflux-transporter reporters. Test whether low drug accumulation, rather than target-level differences, explains which cells survive.

ideas.title: Single-cell multiome of chromatin priming before and during treatment
ideas.description: Profile paired ATAC and RNA in drug-naive cells and at early drug timepoints to find accessible-chromatin states and transcription factor motifs that predict survival. Validate top factors by perturbing them and measuring survival.

ideas.title: Mitochondrial heteroplasmy and OXPHOS heterogeneity in survivors
ideas.description: Sequence mtDNA and image membrane potential and respiration in sorted survivor and dying populations. Test whether naturally varying mitochondrial genotype or function among genetically identical nuclear genomes sets drug tolerance.

candidates: Lineage barcoding (e.g., CellTag or lentiviral barcodes) combined with drug exposure to see whether survivors are clonally related
Longitudinal scRNA-seq of drug-naive cells to find transcriptional states that predict later survival
Single-cell ATAC-seq or multiome before and after drug to find chromatin states that prime survival
Live-cell reporter tracking of fate (fractional killing) linked to pre-treatment reporter levels
BH3 profiling of individual subpopulations to measure apoptotic priming before drug exposure
Per-cell intracellular drug concentration via fluorescent drug analogs or mass-spec imaging, to test uptake and efflux
ABCB1 or other efflux-transporter expression sorting, followed by drug challenge and regrowth
Mitochondrial DNA heteroplasmy and membrane potential heterogeneity measured in sorted survivors
Single-cell proteomics or mass cytometry of stress-response and proteostasis capacity (HSPs, NRF2, ATF4)
Pooled CRISPRi/CRISPRa screen with survival sorting to find regulators of tolerance state
Drug-pulse and washout experiments to test whether tolerance is reversible or epigenetically stable
Histone-mark profiling (H3K27me3, H3K4me3) of sorted survivors to test epigenetic memory
Cell-cycle reporter (FUCCI) and drug-timing experiments to test whether G1 or quiescence determines survival
Paracrine protection assays with conditioned media and co-culture of survivors with sensitive cells
3D spheroid spatial transcriptomics to test whether position in microenvironment gradients determines survival
Single-cell metabolic imaging (NADH FLIM, glucose uptake reporters) to measure metabolic state per cell
Single-cell DNA-seq to detect low-frequency pre-existing ecDNA or copy-number variation among 'identical' cells
Target engagement measured per cell (e.g., single-cell CETSA or drug-bound target fraction) to test whether drug actually reaches its target
DNA damage and replication-stress reporters (53BP1, RPA foci) compared between survivors and dying cells
Nuclear mechanics and chromatin compaction measured by imaging, correlated with survival
Stochastic gene expression noise (smFISH or dual-reporter promoter-noise measurements) of key survival genes
Ribosome profiling or puromycin incorporation per cell to measure translation rate heterogeneity
